title: Syllable Split
rule: When two consonants sit between two vowels (VCCV), divide the word between the consonants.
trickText: Find the two vowels. Look at the consonants between them. Draw the dividing line between those two consonants. Then read each part.
say: Today's case: syllable split. When a word has two consonants between two vowels, we divide between the consonants. Tap the space where the line goes.

example.answer: n a p | k i n
example.say: Look at napkin. There are two vowels, a and i. Two consonants, p and k, sit between them. I divide between the p and the k. Nap, kin.

activities.instruction: Tap the space between the two consonants to divide the word.
